newsitem.title: USA: Arlington, Va., passes $72.9 million GOs.
newsitem.headline: Arlington, Va., passes $72.9 million GOs.

text.p: Voters in Arlington County, Va., overwhelmingly passed four general obligation bond proposals for schools, streets, parks and metro rail, Charlotte Cleary, the county's general registrar, said Wednesday.

The voters in the Washington, D.C. suburb passed the $29.1 million in GOs for the schools by 79 percent with 51,891 voting yes and 14,063 voting no, Cleary said, noting the results were still unofficial.
The $21.3 million GOs for streets and conservation passed by 78 percent with 51,305 voting yes and 14,109 voting no, Cleary said.
The $12.9 million for partks passed by 66 percent with 43,658 voting yes and 22,933 voting no.
And the $9.6 million in GOs for the Metrorail passed with 77 percent or 50,426 voters approving and 14,797 disapproving, Cleary said.
The $29.1 million in schoold funds will be used for a "school renewal program" for the 17,839 student district, said David Miller, the county's capital budget coordinator.
About $6 million of the school GOs is earmarked for a new elementary school in the southern part of the county and the rest for refurbishing and rewiring existing schools, Miller said.
In the park bonds, $8.5 million in budgeted to acquire land for Arlington's open space master plan, said Miller.
